newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold demand likely to rise in September.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold demand likely to rise in September.

text.p: South Korea's domestic gold demand is expected to pick up in September for wedding season, bullion dealers said on Tuesday.
"We expect the gold demand will rise next month as the wedding season comes," said a trader with Tong Yang Global.
Gold demand had been hit by an economic slowdown, a series of corporate defaults and low seasonal demand.
But South Korean demand for legally imported gold has recently increased during the summer as sharply falling gold prices on international markets depressed smuggled gold imports, he said.
"The decline in world bullion prices led smugglers to face falling profits," another trader said.
Traders said unfavourable weather during the summer also contributed to reducing illegal gold imports as bad weather prevented smugglers from using vessels to carry their bullion.
Gold smuggling is rampant in South Korea.
Traders said gold sales from North Korea rose in August but gave no comparison figures.

North Korean gold sales had fallen sharply since the hunger-stricken country sold 1.7 tonnes of gold valued at $19.81 million in April to help finance a party to mark the birthday of the late leader Kim Il-sung.
"North Korea's gold sales seemed to return to normal this month as the nation needed more dollars to buy food for its people," said a trader with a major bullion house.
The daily selling price of domestic gold producer LG Metals, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Tuesday to 9,700 won per gram from 9,800 won a week ago.
The company's silver price rose to 145 won per gram from 143 won a week earlier.

The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers posted by the Korea Exchange Bank fell on Tuesday to 901.00 won against the dollar from 896.50 won a week earlier. The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for bullion companies.
